claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total deterministic-field family defined by proof.md and family.py. At actual length N enumerate primes2<=k<=N, r=ceil(N/k) and r-1 with r>=3,k>r+1, m=min(N,rk), ignored p=N-m, and2<=t<r. Use d=H+E0+1 from disperser.md Sections12--13, B=t(t+3)/2<=d<m, and choose the minimum(4p+8d-4B-3,k,t,p) including the zero option(4N,0,0,0). Construct Q_k by the supplied deterministic prime-degree specialization of Shoup in proof.md Appendix A and irreducible_prime(k), ignore p actual input bits, and evaluate the descending-power order-t symmetric polynomial on the remaining m bits over F2[Z]/Q_k with zero padding. No field-polynomial bits or advice are inputs.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"This ONE fixed total deterministic-field language is in uniform P, hence NP with empty witnesses. The complete prime-degree field construction is supplied in proof.md Appendix A. PRIME-DEGREE coefficient isolation/zero-deficit selection and full-B2 elimination establish C_B2(F_N)>=4N-L_N at EVERY actual integer N>=0 for the exact selector in family.py. Sections8--10 prove L_N<=(1148853/100000)N^(4/5) for EVERY integer N>=0, and L_N<(1148853/100000)N^(4/5)-6N^(3/5) for EVERY integer N>=2^29. Thus C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(1148853/100000)N^(4/5)+6N^(3/5) at every integer N>=2^29. Choosing the better of j=floor(sqrt(r)) and j+1 in the original sufficient threshold gives E<=k*sqrt(r)-k/2-r^(3/2)/4+k/(2sqrt(r))+r/4 in the analytic regime r>1512 and k>r^(3/2); the proof discharges these guards and normalized correction universally. The retained nu8kernel(all30030cells) and two supplied rational kernels(all1441440cells each and tails) prove simultaneous explicit17/20-power-error psi bounds and a prime in(x,(10333/10000)x] for EVERY real x>=2^200. Full coverage uses zero0..195,4954checked intervals196..2^29-1,4619independently certified primes covering EVERY real h in2^17..2^201 for the ENTIRE middle2^29<=N<2^334, and analytic tailN>=2^334. Every emitted prime has independent trial division or a supplied proved Proth witness. Additionally, the SAME family satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(1148853/100000)N^(4/5)+(327/50)N^(3/5) at EVERY integer N>=2^65, by exact refined K1/g1 constants. Universal transfers are supplied proofs, not sample extrapolation. Consequently for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large integer N, C_B2(F_N)>=(4-epsilon)N. The four six-entry tuples compare numeric certified losses only. No prior verdict, floating-point optimum or unsupported nonstandard external theorem is a premise.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: For every ODD PRIME k>=3, the exact irreducible_prime(k) algorithm in family.py terminates in polynomial time in k and outputs a monic irreducible binary polynomial of degree k. proof.md Appendix A supplies the complete prime-degree construction and proof, including binary factor extraction, cyclotomic nonresidue lifting, Kummer extension and trace descent. This specializes a known Shoup construction and does not claim a new general irreducible-construction algorithm.

The complete finite certified losses(original,weighted,positive-exact,zero-deficit,compressed,new) are(1461,1437,1429,1413,1393,1257) at N=500,(2533,2493,2485,2485,2465,2265) at N=1000,(4513,4449,4433,4417,4397,4061) at N=2000,and(16809,16601,16577,16521,16501,15365) at N=10000. These compare certified losses, not actual optimal circuit sizes.

For EVERY integer N>=0 the SAME fixed uniform P family satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(1148853/100000)N^(4/5). Sections8--10 supply the full finite floor/error/prime proof, zero range,4954checked intervals for196..2^29-1,4619prime-chain entries and analytic tail. Every real/integer transfer is proved.

For EVERY integer N>=2^29 the SAME fixed uniform P family satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(1148853/100000)N^(4/5)+6N^(3/5). The target already enumerates j=floor(sqrt(r)) and j+1; Section9 proves that one has original threshold at most H+k*sqrt(r)-k/2-r^(3/2)/4+k/(2sqrt(r))+r/4+1. Complete guards, adjacent-choice proof, normalized g1/K1 estimates and exact constants are supplied. Bounded checks are sanity checks, not the universal premise.

For EVERY integer N>=2^65 the SAME fixed uniform P family satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(1148853/100000)N^(4/5)+(327/50)N^(3/5). The complete adjacent-choice proof, v>=649/500, exact upper root u2278596059/2000000000, increasing K1 and zeta<=1/8192 give K1-g1*zeta-(13/4)zeta^3>327/400. Section9 supplies the whole universal transfer; exact checks support its constants and bounded predicates.
